RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel can reflect organizational blind spots or affinity bias, but on its own, it does not prove unlawful discrimination. For a director role, hiring committees often weigh public consultation, political navigation, and interview performance heavily alongside technical credentials.

Do not raise the panel's composition directly yet. First, follow up politely on your written feedback request; public sector scoring rubrics and notes are often accessible through open records laws. You should only raise the issue if municipal policy strictly mandates diverse panels or if disclosed records show unjustified scoring disparities. Consider consulting an employment attorney before making formal allegations.
